ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, points W, R, T, Z are all on the circle, and they are connected by line segments WR, RT, TZ, ZW to form the inscribed quadrilateral W-R-T-Z. In the figure, an angle of 45° is marked at point W; this is the interior angle of the quadrilateral at vertex W. The problem asks to find m∠T, that is, the interior angle of the same inscribed quadrilateral at vertex T. Then reason: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary. ∠W and ∠T are a pair of opposite angles, so m∠W + m∠T = 180°. Given m∠W = 45°, therefore m∠T = 180° - 45° = 135°.

Since ∠W and ∠T are opposite, m∠T = 180° - 45° = 135°.
